title: Pork & Holy Basil Stir-fry
intro: Also known as Pad Kra Pao, this a popular Thai dish that is actually very simple to cook up.
steps: Prepare the chilli paste by grinding chilli padi and garlic in a mortar and pestle. Adjust the quantities according to your own spice tolerance. Using a food processor or simply mincing it with a knife are possible alternatives
Heat a dash oil in a pan and fry the chilli paste for about a minute or two. Do avoid getting the fumes in your eyes
Add the pork mince and break it up well and allow to brown evenly
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce and soy sauce according to taste and mix well
Once the mince is cooked, turn off the heat add stir basil leaves through the stir-fry
closingRemarks: Best served over rice alongside a fried egg. Pork mince can be replaced with mince or chunks of other protein like chicken or beef. Firm tofu could also work as a meat-free option. Holy basil can be hard to fine, in which case regular basil works fine.

title: Egg Fried Rice
intro: Honestly one of the most versatile meals you can have. Essentially any and i mean ANY ingredient can be added to the base dish, whether it be your choice of protein or any leftover veg you have in the fridge.
steps: Heat some oil in a pan and start cooking your choice of protein or whatever ingredients you wish to add if any. If using scallions/spring onions, the white sections can be added here
Push your ingredients to the side and crack an egg or two into the pan
Allow the egg(s) to set for a few seconds before breaking them up and incorporating them with the rest of your ingredients
Add rice, preferably leftover day old rice, but cooked rice works as well
Add light soy sauce around the edge of the pan and continue to mix till your rice is evenly mixed with the rest of the ingredients. Add any other seasoning here as well
Add the green sections of your scallions/spring onions and mix
closingRemarks: Especially good way to clear leftover rice from previous meals. My personal favourite additions to the base version are tuna, kimchi and an additional egg on top to create a korean-inspired fried rice that also takes less than 15 minutes to prepare and make.

title: Pork and Crab Meatballs
intro: A family favourite I manages to learn from my grandmother; She usually makes a big batch of them leading into Chinese New Year to compliment our many steamboat/hotpot reunion meals.
steps: In a large mixing bowl, add all the listed ingredients and mix well
Knead the mixture and let firm in the fridge for about 30 minutes
Heat up a pot of water or soup/stock
Oil your hands and form the mixture into balls each approximately the size of a ping pong ball
Let the meatballs cook till they float, fish them out and let them cool
closingRemarks: The meatballs can be stored in the fridge or freezer for a few days or weeks respectively. Simply heating them up in some soup is enough. Pairs well with anything to rice, soups and noodles

title: Milk Tea
intro: This is the simpler version of two recipes I've tried and honestly results in milk tea very similar to ones you can get from the stores
steps: In a pot on medium heat, bring the milk to a soft simmer
Add the tea leaves and let steep for 2 minutes
Add the sugar and stir for about a minute until the sugar has dissolved
Turn off the heat and let cool for a bit
Strain the tea and serve either hot or cold
closingRemarks: This can satisfy your milk tea cravings in honestly under 10 minutes. If you do not have loose tea leaves or a sieve/strainer, you could just use teabags. If you wish to elevate it further, you can steep the leaves in minimal water first, before dissolving in the sugar and lastly the milk.

title: Mac & Cheese
intro: This used to be my favourite food back in kindergarten. Looking back, it was definitely less cheesy and more like fried macaroni with cheese slapped on it, but know after trying the 'actual' dish, I still enjoy it quite a bit.
ingredients: Choice of toppings eg. Bread crumbs, Bacon bits
steps: Boil and cook your choice of pasta to al dente. Continue to next steps while waiting
In another pot or deep pan, melt some butter/heat up some oil
Add an equal amount of flour and mix to form a roux. Let the flour cook out but be careful not to burn the roux
Slowly add the milk in, consistently stirring to incorporate it with the roux, eventually making a bechamel sauce
Add in your choice of cheeses and season it well to form your cheese sauce
Mix your cheese sauce into your pasta and transfer to a large baking dish
Add your toppings and finish with another layer of cheese if you like
Bake at 200°C until the top is golden brown
closingRemarks: Good sharing meal to accompany other side dishes

title: Corned Beef Silog
intro: This Filipino breakfast classic is really quick to make and pretty filling too.
steps: Start off by frying an egg in oil to your desired doneness. I prefer mine with a runny yolk
Set aside the egg; Saute your diced garlic and onions in the remaining oil till fragrant
Add your corned beef and continue cooking

You can add a small amount of broth and season with salt and pepper here, but I find the corned beef I get sufficiently salty on its own. I also let the beef crisp up on the bottom before moving it around for added texture
Serve with some fried or plain rice with the fried egg on top. Garnish with spring onions if you have it
closingRemarks: Quick hearty breakfast for lazy people like me, especially if you have leftover rice which you can also quickly heat up. Nothing is stopping you from stir frying with some veg on the side or with the beef as well.

title: Shakshuka
intro: A popular North African meal that is surprisingly as healthy as it is delicious
steps: Chop your bell peppers and onion and cook in a large pan with olive oil for till onion becomes translucent (about 5 minutes)
Add garlic and the spices and continue cooking for a bit
Pour in the can of tomatoes/diced fresh tomatoes and break them apart with a large spoon or spatula
Season with salt and pepper and bring the sauce to a simmer
Make a few divots/wells in the sauce and crack your eggs in them. Cover with a lid and let cook to your desired egg doneness
Garnish with chopped cilantro/parsley or both
Eat as is or serve with bread or rice
closingRemarks: Really easy way to pack lots of vegetables into a meal. The base (without eggs) is also easily kept as leftovers or frozen to be reheated later. You could also add your choice of protein like mince for a heartier meal.

title: Chawanmushi
intro: A simple egg custard dish that is a staple in Japanese cuisine. It is often served as a side dish or appetizer and can be made with various ingredients.
ingredients: Choice of fillings (e.g., shrimp, chicken, mushrooms, ginkgo nuts, Narutomaki (fishcake))
steps: Heat up a pot of water to create a steaming environment
In a bowl, add eggs and dashi with a ratio of 1 to 2.5 or 3. 2.5 gives an eggier flavour while 3 gives a more delicate texture
Add an equal amount of soy sauce, mirin, and sake to the egg mixture. Adjust according to taste
To your serving bowls, add your choice of fillings and strain the egg mixture into them, being careful to remove any bubbles or foam
Cover the bowls with aluminum foil or a lid and steam for 15 minutes on a gentle heat, 20 minutes if a meat filling is used
Check for doneness by inserting a toothpick or skewer into the custard; a clear liquid should come out and the skewer should come out clean
closingRemarks: Very simple and versatile dish that can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature. It can be made with various fillings and I enjoy it alongside other Japanese dishes I make such as Soba or Japanese stirfry dishes and rice.

title: Ajitama (Ramen Egg)
intro: Marinated eggs that are often served with ramen, but can also be enjoyed on their own as a snack or side dish.
steps: To a pot of boiling water, add your eggs straight from the fridge and let sit for 6-7 minutes for a soft-boiled egg
Remove the eggs and immediately submerge them in an ice bath to stop the cooking process

In another saucepan, add an equal amount of soy sauce, mirin, and sake to create the marinade. Gently heat the mixture to boil of the alcohol. Dissolving sugar in the marinade is optional. Sake can be replaced with an equal amount of water
Once the eggs are cooled, gently peel them and place them in a container
Pour the marinade over the eggs, ensuring they are fully submerged. If not, you can flip them halfway through the marinating process
closingRemarks: Able to be kept in the fridge for up to a week; Perfect for meal prep or to have on hand for a quick snack. I usually make this at the start of the week if I am planning to make ramen the following week

title: Tonkotsu Ramen
intro: A simple quick cheat version of Tonkotsu ramen that still delivers on flavour and mouthfeel.
ingredients: Dashi Stock (Any other stock can be used as well)
Choice of toppings (e.g., Nori sheet, Ramen eggs, Chashu pork, Menma (bamboo shoots), Scallions, Narutomaki (fishcake))
steps: In a pot, heat some oil and start frying off the pork belly
Add minced garlic and continue frying till fragrant

Add dashi stock, soy milk, soy sauce, mirin, sake, oyster sauce to the pot and bring to a simmer. The exact amounts can be adjusted according to taste but for a single serving, I usually use 1 cup of dashi and soy milk each, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of mirin, 1 teaspoon of sake and oyster sauce
In a separate pot, cook your ramen noodles according to the package instructions
Once the noodles are cooked, drain them and add them to your serving bowl and mix with a drizzle of sesame oil
Pour the broth over the noodles and top with your choice of toppings
closingRemarks: This is a quick and easy way to make a delicious bowl of ramen at home. The use of almond or soy milk gives the broth a creamy texture without the need for hours of simmering pork bones. I usually make this when I am craving ramen and already have some Ajitama eggs prepared in the fridge.

title: Sardine Bee Hoon
intro: Recipe I got from my mother's friend. It feels like a very homey dish that is quick to make and very comforting.
ingredients: Choice of Vegetables (e.g., Carrots, Choy Sum, Spinach, or any leafy greens)
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in hot water for about 10 minutes or until softened. Drain and set aside
In a large pan or wok, heat some oil and sauté minced garlic, diced onion, and chopped chili padi until fragrant
Add the canned sardines with their sauce to the pan and break them up gently
Add a splash of water and the vegetables of your choice, and let them cook down for a few minutes
Add some sugar and ketchup to taste, adjusting the sweetness and tanginess according to your preference
Add the soaked rice vermicelli to the pan and toss everything together until well combined and heated through
Cover with a lid to let the bee hoon absorb the flavors for a few minutes
Serve hot, garnished with additional fried shallots and/or sambal chili
closingRemarks: The dish is honestly carried by the canned sardines as well as the sauce they come in. The bee hoon soaks up all the flavours and is a great way to use up leftover vegetables in the fridge.

title: Pig Trotter Bee Hoon
intro: A dish I used to have alot as a child. Also a favourite of my family. I kind of improvised this recipe based on my memory of how it tasted.
ingredients: Choice of Vegetables (e.g., Cabbage, Choy Sum, Bell Peppers/Capsicum, or any leafy greens)
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli and mushrooms in hot water for about 10 minutes or until softened.
In a large pan or wok, heat some oil and sauté minced garlic until fragrant
Add the vegetables of your choice, mushrooms and sauté for a few minutes
Add the canned braised pig trotters with their sauce to the pan.
Add a splash of water, oyster sauce, and light soy sauce to taste, adjusting the seasoning according to your preference
Add the soaked rice vermicelli to the pan and toss everything together until well combined and heated through
Cover with a lid to let the bee hoon absorb the flavors for a few minutes
Serve hot, garnished with additional fried shallots and/or sambal chili
closingRemarks: Felt great to recreate this dish after so many years, with the help of input from my mother and grandmother. Apparently, the bones from the trotters can be blended and inciorporated into the sauce to make it thicker and richer, but I was unable to do it as my hand blender was not powerful enough. Attempting it broke my hand blender lol

title: Chicken Puffs
intro: A little something I tried after getting my hands on puff pastry for the first time. Kind of trial and error but turned out well
steps: Preheat your oven to 200°C
In a pan, heat some oil and sauté minced garlic and diced onion until fragrant
Add diced carrots and mushrooms and continue cooking till they soften
Add shredded chicken and a few spoonfuls of cream of mushroom soup to bind the filling together. Season with salt and pepper to taste
Roll out your puff pastry and cut into squares of your desired size
Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of each square
Fold the pastry over to form a triangle or rectangle and seal the edges by pressing with a fork
Brush the tops with egg wash for a golden finish
Bake at 200°C in oven for 20-25 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed up. Timing will depend on the size of your puffs
closingRemarks: First time working with puff pastry. Definetely alot more efficient than trying to make it from scratch. Using campbell mushroom soup mix also helps add flavour and creaminess to the filling. Veg choices are flexible. For an even easier version, you could use rotisserie chicken as well.

title: Oyakodon
intro: Simple and nutritional meal that is not only quick to make but also flavourful
steps: Create the sauce by mixing dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a bowl or straight in the pan/pot. I usualyy eyeball everything and adjust it as I go along
Slice onions and chicken into bite-sized pieces. Chicken thighs are preferred, but chicken breast can be used as well, just care not to overcook them
Add everthing into the pan/pot and bring to a simmer. Let the chicken cook through and the onions soften
Lightly beat the eggs in a bowl. No need to fully mix, leaving some streaks of egg white is fine to provide more colour contrast

Once the chicken is mostly cooked, pour half the egg mixture evenly over the chicken and cover with a lid and allow to set. Pour the rest of the egg mixture and cover again, turning off the heat and letting the residual heat set a little or to desired doneness. I prefer it more runny
Serve over rice and garnish with chopped scallions/spring onions if you have them
closingRemarks: Simple go to meal that takes minimal effort and time. I usually default to this when I have leftover rice. Chicken can be replaced with other meats like pork belly/collar, beef etc. but I find chicken thigh to be the best fit.

title: Homemade Pizza
intro: First thing I made after getting my oven some time ago. Hardest part is just getting the dough right, but once you have that down, the rest is pretty straightforward
ingredients: Choice of toppings (Cheese, Pepperoni, Bell Peppers/Capsicum, Onions, Mushrooms, Ham etc.)
steps: Honestly, there are many recipes online for pizza dough. The few times I made it, I used different recipes each time, but I don't really see much big difference between them. Generally, you will need flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water and some oil. Mix everything together and knead the dough till it is smooth and elastic. Let it proof in a warm place till it doubles in size. I usually have it develop overnight in the fridge though
Preheat your oven to the highest temperature it can go, usually around 250°C. Important to have the baking tray heated as well to get a good cook on the bottom
Roll out the dough to desired shape, thickness and size.
Spread a thin layer of pizza sauce over the dough. Honestly, a little goes a long way
Add your choice of toppings
Bake in the oven for about 10-15 minutes or until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly and slightly browned
closingRemarks: Surprisingly fun but messy process. I usually make it when flour is about to expire. Technically, dough can be made in advance and frozen but I end up eating it all within 2 days so I don't bother.  I prefer a simple margherita style pizza with just cheese and basil. Accidentally made it with expired flour and yeast once and it still turned out fine. Dough didn't rise as much but it was still edible. Had to roll it out a lot thinner as the dough was significantly denser

title: Marinara Sauce
intro: Versatile sauce that can be used for pasta, pizza, dipping sauce
steps: Heat some olive oil in a pan and sauté minced garlic and diced onion until fragrant
Deglaze the pan with a splash of water or white wine if you have it
Add canned tomatoes and break them up with a spoon or spatula if required
Add dried oregano, sugar and basil bouquet.
Let the sauce simmer for about 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally. If the sauce becomes too thick, add a bit of water to reach your desired consistency
closingRemarks: Can be used for meal prep. Keeps well in the fridge for up to a week or can be frozen for longer storage. Made a batch recently which contributed to my homemade pizza and pasta dishes

title: Smoked Duck Pasta
intro: Pasta variant that utilises smoked duck breast. Hearty, food coma inducing meal
steps: Prepare smoked duck breast according to package instructions. Usually involves pan searing the skin side to render the fat and crisp it up or simply microwaving it. I usually use precooked frozen ones but fresh ones should work as well
Cook your pasta according to package instructions
In another pot or deep pan, melt some butter/heat up some oil
Sauté minced garlic and diced onion until soften. Either dice it up fine or blend it to a paste if you prefer a less chunky sauce
Add an equal amount of flour and mix to form a roux. Let the flour cook out but be careful not to burn the roux. letting it brown a little is fine
Slowly add the milk in, consistently stirring to incorporate it with the roux, eventually making a bechamel sauce
Add Italian herbs and season with salt and pepper to taste
Mix your bechamel sauce into your pasta and add sliced smoked duck breast. Mix in some of the duck fat if you rendered it earlier for added flavour
Serve with some grated parmesan cheese if you have it. Alternatively, cheese can be added into the sauce as well
closingRemarks: Essentially some bechamel variant sauce with pasta and duck. Protein can be replaced. Mushrooms and vegetables like spincah and kale can be added as well.

title: Aglio e Olio
intro: Probably up there with one of my most cooked meals at home. Simple, quick and versatile that can be paired with any protein or eaten as is
steps: Starting from a cold pan, add olive oil, garlic (sliced or diced) and red chilli flakes (chopped red chillis can be used too)
On a very low heat, let the ingredients infuse in the oil, making sure not to burn anything
Add a splash of water and the vegetables of your choice, and let them cook down for a few minutes
Cook your pasta according to package instructions

One trick I learnt to get a good emulsified sauce is to add the pasta water straight into the garlic infused oil first and have it emulsify before adding the pasta. I usually add almost as much pasta water as olive oil and stir vigorously over high heat
Once the sauce has achieved desired consistency, add the cooked pasta and toss to coat. At this pointm you can turn the heat off and add your choice of cooked protein if you have any
Finish with chopped parsley or other italian herbs you have on hand
closingRemarks: In the iamge, I paired it with oven baked salmon which I flaked after cooking as well as the crispy salmon skin for more texture. Usually I would have this as is or with shrimp if I have them on hand. Some may add cheese to it but I prefer it without especially not with seafood

title: Miso Chicken
intro: A good alternative to the standard chicken seasoned with just salt and pepper. Sweet and savoury that imparts great flavour.
steps: To make the sauce, combine miso paste, mirin, sake and sugar. Soy sauce can also be added but I usually omit it since my miso is salty enough
Add your chicken thighs to the marinade and let sit for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is preferred to let the flavour penetrate the chicken better
Remove the chicken from the marinade and pat dry. This is where the longer marinating time helps because the surface marinade has to be removed due to it burning very easily from the sugar content

Starting from a cold pan, add the chicken thighs skin side down and let it cook on low heat to render the fat and crisp up the skin. I usually cover it with parchment paper and add a weight on top to ensure even contact with the pan. Sometimes, if there's too much fat, you can remove it with a paper towel. Less oil ironically also helps the skin crisp up better
The chicken will be mostly cooked through by the time the skin is crispy. Flip it over and cook the other side for a minute or two to finish
Let the chicken rest for a few minutes before slicing and serving. The leftovered marinade can be boiled down with some water to make a sauce to drizzle over the chicken if desired
Best served over rice with a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Vegetables work too
closingRemarks: Honestly, I feel like the sauce is flexible enough to be paired with other meats, but nothing beats a good crispy chicken thigh.

title: Chicken Parm
intro: Very helpful for using up cheese especially for people that cook for themselves only :( and can never justify buying a whole block of cheese
steps: Butterfly and pound the chicken breast till its even in thickness throughout
Set up a pane station and do the standard flour, egg, panko/breadcrumbs coating
Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry the chicken till golden brown on both sides
Transfer the chicken to a baking dish. Top with tomato sauce and cheese (any of the typical cheese can work but the melty ones like mozzarella are preferred for that cheese pull)
Bake/Broil in the oven till the cheese is melted and just about golden brown
closingRemarks: My sister really enjoyed this one when I made it for lunch. Pairs well with pasta. I would have made something like aglio e olio for more variation in flavour but pasta tossed in the same marinara sauce works too

title: Parmagiana Di Melanzane
intro: Eggplant; a childhood nightmare for me. Never really liked it. This was part of an attempt to give it another go so what better way than to douse it in marinara sauce and cheese?
steps: Slice the eggplant into thin rounds, salt them and let sit for 20-30 minutes to draw out as much moisture as possible. Pat dry with paper towels
Set up a pane station and do the standard flour, egg, panko/breadcrumbs coating. Breading is optional and can be replaced with just a light dusting a flour if you prefer
Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry the eggplant slices till golden brown on both sides

Transfer the fried eggplant slices to a baking dish. Top with tomato sauce and cheese. Can also do some kind of layering like lasagna if you have enough eggplant slices and the baking dish is too small
closingRemarks: Honestly the first time I tried it, I didn't really like. When I went back for more I realised the flesh is honestly fine. It was probably the eggplant skin that imparts that acrid and overly bittter taste that I was aversive too. If I were to make this again I would proably peel the eggplant first. But truthfully speaking, I would probably just go down the chicken parm route instead

title: Chicken with Mustard Sauce
intro: Honestly a random concoction I made. Originally I wanted to do a french style 3 ingredient dish (chicken, onions and salt) but I didnt have enough onions so I improvised
steps: Salt both sides of the chicken thighs and let sit for 10 to 20 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry with paper towels.

Starting from a cold pan, add the chicken thighs skin side down and let it cook on low heat to render the fat and crisp up the skin. I usually cover it with parchment paper and add a weight on top to ensure even contact with the pan. Sometimes, if there's too much fat, you can remove it with a paper towel. Less oil ironically also helps the skin crisp up better
The chicken will be mostly cooked through by the time the skin is crispy. Flip it over and cook the other side for a minute or two to finish. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside
In the same pan, add diced onions/shallots and minced garlic and sauté till fragrant and softened
Add a spoonful or two of dijon mustard and mix well
Add cream or milk to loosen the sauce and bring to a simmer. Adjust the amount of mustard and cream/milk according to taste
Return the chicken to the pan and coat it with the sauce. Let it simmer for a minute to reheat the chicken
Serve with rice or pasta or as is
closingRemarks: Really happy with how it turned out. Really simple meal too. My one gripe was not having any other sides or carbs to go along with it the one time I made it. Definitely making this again whenever I can

title: Omurice
intro: Simple dish using the same ingredients as egg fried rice and if you want to spend more time in the kitchen like I usually do
steps: Fry your rice however you like it. Typical process would be cook your proteins and vegetables before adding rice and then seasoning it
The choice of sauce is flexible. You can go for the standard light soy sauce or try the ketchup and tokatsu sauce as alternatives for a sweeter flavour profile
Once your fried rice is done, set it aside and prepare to make the omelette
In a bowl, beat 2-3 eggs per serving and season with salt
Heat up oil and/or butter in a pan and pour in the eggs once hot
I usually aggresively swirl the eggs to create curds for abit before letting it set slightly
I like my eggs very runny so I would get to folding it pretty quickly but you can cook it till whatever doneness you prefer
You can either fold the egg over the rice in the pan itself or transfer the fried rice onto a plate and then place the omelette on top
closingRemarks: To be completely honest I would probably still cook a standard egg fried ricve over this since its faster and less fuss. That said, I would probably cook thhis if I ever make a demi glace sauce to try a different variation of omurice

title: Bibimbap (but not really)
intro: Really craving bibimbap one day but no gochujang or gochugaru in sight, so I attempted an improvised japanese-style bibimbap using miso paste instead
steps: Chop your vegetables
For things like carrots, you can leave them raw or give a quick saute. For leafy greens, I like to blanch them briefly then toss with sesame seeds and sesame oil with a pinch of salt
Fried off some pork mince some garlic and salt till cooked though

To make the miso sauce, to a pot, gently heat miso paste and the classic japanese trinity of soy sauce, mirin and sake. Adjust the amounts according to taste. Can also add some sugar to balance it out. Add a bit of water to loosen the sauce if needed
To a bed of rice, add the all the toppings and finish with a fried or poached egg on top
Drizzle the miso sauce over the bowl and mix everything together before eating
closingRemarks: really good way to get vegetables in though it does take alot of chopping since the dish is mostly prep work. I just happened to make a simmered enoki mushroon dish (Nametake) that day so I added that as well.

title: Pumpkin Sauce
intro: Part 2 of trying vegetables I used to dislike. This time pumpkin. Tried making it into a sauce this time
steps: Cut the vegetables into chunks and season with salt, pepper and oil
Roast in the oven at 200°C till soft
Once done, remove from oven and let cool slightly before blending with cream or milk until smooth
closingRemarks: Nothing really much to it. Just a simple roasted pumpkin sauce that I finished with pasta. Honestly, I feel it works better as a soup/chowder rather than as a sauce.

title: Mapo Tofu
intro: My new go to meal that can be prepared in under 15 minutes. Adjustable spice levels and pairs well with rice and noodles
steps: In a pan, heat some oil and brown the ground meat. I like to sear it on each side first before breaking it up to get some extra texture and crisp on the meat
Add minced garlic and continue cooking till fragrant, the whites of the scallions/spring onions if you have them can be added in at this point as well

Add a spoonful of doubanjiang and chilli crisp oil to taste. Adjust the amount according to your spice preference. I would assume fresh chilli or the traditional Sichuan peppercorns would be added here as well if you have them on hand
Add a splash of water to loosen the sauce and let it simmer for a bit. I usually add some chicken bouillion powder to season as well, but classic salt and white pepper works too
In the meantime, cut your silken tofu into cubes and add them to the pan. Be careful when stirring to avoid breaking up the tofu too much
To thicken the sauce, mix some flour with water to create a slurry and add it to the pan. Let it cook for an extra minute to let the sauce thicken up to your desired consistency
Serve with rice or noodles and garnish with the greens of the scallions/spring onions if you have them
closingRemarks: Good sharing meal to accompany other side dishes but also works as a main on its own. This has surpassed my previous quick meal fix of oyakodon simply because there is even less prepping to be done, especially since I keep frozen garlic on hand and the ground meat needs no additional processing.
